purpose: Bake three pixel-aligned orthographic atlas maps - face_albedo (pigment RGB + paint-mask alpha), face_normal_depth (tangent normal RGB + normalized height alpha) and face_ao_roughness (cavity AO in R, specular roughness in G) - from true 3D carved tile-face geometry. These are the input of the Task 5A orientation-aware carved-relief shading; the Task 4 flat glyphs remain the runtime fallback until Task 5A lands. Nothing here is a per-orientation sprite: one master face per tile id, lit in world space at runtime.
status: Task 4B: 37 faces (34 standard + 3 red fives) baked at 256 x 340 px into three 1536 x 2380 atlases. Geometry is a displaced face plate (engrave inward, no boolean) with the glyph floor at 0.55 mm and a 40 degree V-carve bevel outside the glyph outline, plus a small hand-carve rounding and depth variation. Maps are rendered by Cycles from an orthographic camera, one master render pass per data group, then packed cell-for-cell into the atlases.
coordinateSpace: Each atlas cell is the inset face plate in face-local space: the cell's top-left is the glyph's top-left, exactly like the flat glyph in faces.json, so the cell maps onto the same shell faceQuad (TL/TR/BR/BL). The plate is 0.64 x 0.89 tile units = 17.92 x 24.92 mm; the 256 x 340 px cell has 14.2857 px/mm across and 13.6434 px/mm down (4.7% texel anisotropy). Normal RGB is tangent x right, y down, z out; the slot basis published by table_layout.json maps it to world space as n.x*T + n.y*B + n.z*N with no sign flip.

upstream.variant: regular symbol-only SVG, 300 x 400 viewBox, transparent background
upstream.license: CC0 1.0 public domain (upstream README: 'All assets are in the public domain')
upstream.notes: The upstream Regular-Blank.svg is a red question mark, not an empty tile face, so it is deliberately not vendored. Haku (5z) is a real face: its symbol-only SVG rasterises to zero ink because a white dragon has no printed symbol.

channels.face_albedo: RGB pure pigment (no baked lighting), #FFFFFF where the paint mask is 0; A paint mask (0 un-carved resin, 1 enamel groove)
channels.face_normal_depth: RGB tangent normal x right / y down / z out; A normalized height (1 un-carved, 0 deepest engraving)
channels.face_ao_roughness: R cavity AO (1 open face, ~0.45 tight junction); G specular roughness (0.45 resin, 0.12 lacquer); B 0; A 255

carve.notes: The groove floor is the glyph area displaced inward by depthMm with a flat bottom; the V-carve bevel sits OUTSIDE the glyph outline over a horizontal run of depth / tan(wallAngle) = 0.655 mm, so the painted silhouette is identical to the flat glyph and the bevel is pure carved ivory that catches the world-locked key light. Height is the union of the carve contributions, i.e. the signed distance to the glyph union drives one ramp, so two strokes closer together than 2x the run merge into a shallow V valley instead of over-cutting.

paint.pigment: glyph RGB (same a60c0c crimson recolour as faces.json; the art's own emerald, prussian and carbon fills are kept)

roughness.notes: 0.45 semi-matte melamine on the un-carved face, 0.12 glossy lacquer inside the painted grooves.

paint.notes: Albedo RGB is the pure pigment with no baked lighting so Task 5A multiplies it onto the lit blank body; it is set to #FFFFFF wherever the paint mask is exactly 0, so un-carved ivory carries neutral white. Albedo alpha is the paint mask, 0.0 on un-carved resin and 1.0 inside painted enamel grooves.

remap.notes: t = clamp((raw - low) / (1 - low), 0, 1); R = floor + (1 - floor) * t^gamma. The raw Cycles visibility only reaches about 0.68-0.85 in these shallow 0.5 mm engravings, so the remap is what turns it into a readable cavity term: the planar open face stays exactly 1.0, a tight stroke junction lands near 0.45-0.50, and the deepest V-corner floors out at 0.25 instead of going black.

ao.notes: Cycles Ambient Occlusion node, only local, 24 rays at 1.2 mm. The baked R channel is the remapped value; the manifest records the raw and mapped min/mean/max it measured. A 3x3 median on the raw visibility removes single-ray self-intersection speckle on the open face (the plate is a single-sided sheet, so grazing rays occasionally clip it).
